responsibility: This module contains GCC’s compiler-side sanitizer subsystem: the GIMPLE/RTL instrumentation, shared builtin definitions, and late optimization/expansion logic that implement dynamic bug-detection and fuzzing support across the middle end. Its main source families provide AddressSanitizer and HWASan memory-checking with shadow memory, stack/global poisoning, redzones, and runtime initialization; ThreadSanitizer instrumentation for memory accesses and synchronization-related events; UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer check insertion plus the metadata and diagnostic payload generation needed to report undefined operations; and SanitizerCoverage hooks for fuzzing-oriented control-flow, comparison, and switch tracing. Supporting headers define the shared sanitizer interfaces and ABI/policy constants, sanitizer.def centralizes the runtime builtin inventory used by these passes, sanopt performs sanitizer-specific deduplication and lowering of internal sanitizer functions into concrete runtime calls and control flow, and gdbasan.in provides debugger support for sanitizer report entry points. Together, this module is responsible for turning GCC IR into instrumented code that cooperates with sanitizer runtimes, distinguishing it from neighboring optimization or target code-generation modules.
